topics.label: Introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: It provides the introductory framing and outlines the learning objectives for the lecture.

topics.label: Viral oncology, cellular oncogenes, and transformation assays
topics.groupedBecause: They trace how the study of tumor viruses revealed cellular proto-oncogenes and established laboratory assays for measuring cell transformation.

topics.label: Oncogenes, tumor suppressor genes, and mutation mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: They define the functional classifications of cancer genes and illustrate how specific mutations in pathways such as Rb and p53 alter cell regulation.

topics.label: Mechanisms and consequences of genomic instability
topics.groupedBecause: They examine how defects in DNA repair, replication fidelity, and mitotic chromosome segregation produce sequence and chromosomal instability.

topics.label: Multistep tumorigenesis and hereditary cancer predisposition
topics.groupedBecause: They explain how the sequential accumulation of somatic and inherited genetic alterations drives cancer initiation and progression.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and reading recommendations
topics.groupedBecause: It provides the closing remarks and suggests further reading following the lecture.
